entities.summary: The Battle of Minden was a major engagement during the Seven Years' War, fought on 1 August 1759. An Anglo-German army under the overall command of Prussian Field Marshal Ferdinand of Brunswick defeated a Franco-Saxon army commanded by Marshal of France, Marquis de Contades. Two years previously, the French had launched a successful invasion of Hanover and attempted to impose an unpopular treaty of peace upon the allied nations of Britain, Hanover and Prussia. After a Prussian victory at Rossbach, and under pressure from Frederick the Great and William Pitt, King George II disavowed the treaty.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Battle of Minden thwarted a Franco-Saxon attempt to impose an unpopular treaty on Britain and Prussia, forcing King George II to reject it after his victory at Rossbach. This event delayed the French occupation of Hanover and preserved British interests in the region.
